rules.disease: pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (PA/VSD/MAPCAs)
rules.sentence: Some studies estimate that pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (PA/VSD/MAPCAs) occurs in approximately 10 out of 100,000 live births.[2]

rules.disease: tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia (pulmonary atresia with VSD)
rules.sentence: This condition often accompanies congenital heart diseases that reduce pulmonary blood flow, like tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia (pulmonary atresia with VSD), though it can also occur by itself on rare occasions.
Such an anomaly is known as an isolated aortopulmonary collateral artery and is a potential cause of congestive heart failure in neonates.[3][4][5]
Children with MAPCAs due to Alagille syndrome have a poor prognosis, mainly due to multiorgan system involvement.[6][7][8]
PA/VSD/MAPCAs is a complex congenital cardiac anomaly that manifests in approximately 10 out of 100,000 live births.
